problem: Turn on the "YouTube Analytics API" in your Google Cloud project, then tap Analyze now again.
summary: Among the 21 films older than 2 days, the strongest are hands-on kitchen and home demos where two identical setups behave differently. They open with a short statement that gives away the surprising result: Paper Bridge 457.2/day, Water Bottle Vortex 436.7/day, Raisin 384.3/day. Space topics, invention history and myth-style questions sit in the bottom group. These are early patterns, not proven causes. Views per day falls as films age, the newer films had a different writer and language setting, and no retention data is available.

working.lesson: Side-by-side home or kitchen demos where two identical setups give opposite results are the top performers.
working.evidence: The top 3 films older than 2 days are all this format: Paper Bridge (flat vs folded) 457.2/day, Water Bottle Vortex (swirled vs not) 436.7/day, Raisin (still vs sparkling water) 384.3/day. The 8 mature kitchen/home experiment films average…

working.lesson: Short statement hooks that reveal the surprising result beat question hooks.
working.evidence: Mature films with statement hooks average 242.6/day across 8 films, including 'Paper holds more coins when you fold it.' (457.2) and 'The swirled bottle empties first.' (436.7). The 3 question hooks average 104.2/day: Moon 95.7, Mpemba 85.…

working.lesson: A practical warning about something the viewer owns can do well.
working.evidence: 'Hot water can crack your frozen windshield.' got 271.8/day, 1,058 views and 18 likes in 3.9 days, the 4th best mature film.

working.lesson: Films of about 29–34 seconds do best.
working.evidence: The 12 mature films of 29–34s average 217.1/day. The 6 films under 29s average 101.2/day, and the 3 films over 34s average 132.8/day. The top 3 films are 29, 30 and 31 seconds long.

working.lesson: Fully animated films (no real photos) did well among mature films. This is an early sign only.

working.lesson: Big, current spectacle news can open strongly. This is an early sign only.
working.evidence: Starship 'landed in midair' has 991 views in 1.7 days (581.0/day), the highest views per day on the channel. It is still growing, so the number is not final.

notWorking.lesson: Space and astronomy explainers without a hands-on demo stay low.
notWorking.evidence: Leonids 45.1/day, Moon Illusion 95.7/day, Voyager 98.9/day, Seasons 147.8/day. Their average is 96.9/day.

notWorking.lesson: Topics tied to a date go stale fast.
notWorking.evidence: The Leonid meteor shower film has the lowest views per day of the mature films except Tightrope: 408 views in 9.1 days, 45.1/day, 2 likes.

notWorking.lesson: Invention-history stories did poorly in their only test.
notWorking.evidence: The melted candy bar microwave origin film got 83.2/day. It was also the only film using AI media, so one film cannot separate the two causes.

notWorking.lesson: 'Is this myth true?' question openings underperform.
notWorking.evidence: Mpemba ('Which freezes first...?') 85.4/day and Moon ('Why does the Moon look huge...?') 95.7/day are both in the bottom half.

rules: Build the film around two identical setups side by side where one behaves unexpectedly, using objects from a normal kitchen or home.
Open with one short statement (under 8 words) that gives the surprising result, e.g. 'The swirled bottle empties first.'
Don't open with a question; state the claim and then prove it on screen.
Aim for 29–34 seconds; avoid going under 28s or over 35s.
Show the result in the first shot, before any explanation.
Pick topics the viewer can test or meets at home or in the car, not distant space facts.
Avoid topics tied to a date or event unless they are huge, current spectacle news.
Put the everyday object and the result in the title, e.g. 'Paper Bridge Test: How Much Can a Fold Hold?'
moreTopics: Kitchen experiments with a twin control (two cups, bottles, sheets or eggs)
Household materials doing something counterintuitive (folding, swirling, fizzing)
Practical home and car safety physics ('don't do X, here's why')
Everyday mechanisms with a hidden trick (zippers, pumps, latches)
Big current engineering spectacles explained with a home analogy
lessTopics: Astronomy events tied to a specific date
Abstract space facts with no hands-on demo (light delay, moon illusion)
Abstract mechanics shown only with animated people (tightrope, brick catch)
hooks: Paper holds more coins when you fold it.
This raisin rises while its twin stays put.
Hot water can crack your frozen windshield.
experiments: Make two kitchen side-by-side films on similar topics, one with a statement hook and one with a question hook, to test whether hook style holds up on its own.
Make the same type of home demo once fully animated and once with real photos, to separate the photo effect from the newer-batch effect.
Post similar films at 14:00 and at 09:00 on the same weekday to get a clean timing comparison; current day and hour data are mixed up with film age.
